patients.summary: Young woman with severe persistent asthma (prior intubation) and allergic rhinitis, uninsured with Medicaid pending, who joins in 2023. Gonococcal cervicitis and then secondary syphilis are treated at outside OB/GYN with practice-run titer follow-up; a community-acquired pneumonia precedes an ICU admission for status asthmaticus that finally steps her up to ICS-LABA.

orders.order: Request records from prior primary care practice

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 yo woman here to establish. Moved her care to us after her old pediatric/adolescent office stopped seeing adults. Works part time waiting tables in town. No insurance right now; Medicaid application started, she has the confirmation letter.

Asthma: since she was little. Says it is 'bad asthma', has been told severe. Uses albuterol a few days most weeks, more with colds and in the spring. Fluticasone 220 one puff BID is prescribed but she admits she takes it 'when I remember, maybe half the time'. Night cough a couple of nights a month. Has a peak flow meter at home, does not use it much. Never been on a combination inhaler that she knows of.
Allergies: seasonal sneezing, itchy eyes in spring and fall; levocetirizine as needed helps.

PMH: asthma, allergic rhinitis. PSH: none. Meds as listed. NKDA.
FH: mother has asthma. A maternal uncle has eczema.
SH: never smoked, no vaping. Drinks a little on weekends, 1-2.

Exam: well, talking in full sentences. HEENT: nasal turbinates mildly pale and boggy, OP clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Lungs: clear, no wheeze, good air movement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abd soft. Skin clear.

A/P
1. Severe persistent asthma, partly controlled. The main issue is adherence to the controller. Talked through why the fluticasone matters even on good days, linked it to brushing teeth. Spacer technique reviewed. Refill albuterol and fluticasone. Return 4 mo, sooner if using albuterol more than twice a week.
2. Allergic rhinitis: levocetirizine prn, ok.
3. Health maintenance: hep C screen today with baseline CBC/BMP. Will get vaccine and Pap history from prior office. Flu/COVID/pneumococcal in the fall.
PHQ-2 negative.

documents.title: Result note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with lab results per PCP: blood counts, kidney function and sugar normal, hep C screen negative. She verbalized understanding. Release form for her prior office signed at check-in yesterday, faxed today.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
28 pages received by fax from prior pediatric and adolescent office. Contents: immunization record (childhood series complete; HPV series x3 completed age 12-13; hepatitis B series complete in infancy; Tdap 2019), problem list (asthma, allergic rhinitis), asthma visit notes, Pap 10/2022 negative. Scanned to media tab, routed to PCP.

PCP addendum: reviewed. Vaccines entered. Pap due again fall 2025.

documents.title: inhaler price
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hi the pharmacy said the fluticasone is sooo expensive without insurance?? i can't do that right now. the albuterol was ok with the coupon. is there anything cheaper

documents.title: RE: inhaler price
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jada, thanks for telling me rather than just going without. Our MA is going to send you a discount card link that brings the generic fluticasone down a lot at most chain pharmacies, and I put a note on your Medicaid paperwork that it's a daily medicine. Please don't stretch it out. If it is still too much, message back and we'll find another way.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after her lunch shift for vaccines. Afebrile, feels well. Flu L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, PCV20 L deltoid lower site (asthma indication, per PCP order). VIS sheets given. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Pt reminded about controller inhaler every day; says she is doing better with it, keeps it by the coffee maker.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request from pharmacy for albuterol HFA. Last fill 6 weeks ago. Fluticasone last filled in August per pharmacy. Albuterol approved per protocol; message to PCP about the controller gap.

documents.title: Controller gap
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt about fluticasone not filled since August. She ran out and was 'waiting till payday'. Discount card info re-sent by text. She will pick up both today. Reminded to call if using albuterol daily.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily for 5 days

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (received 01/16/2024)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Department of Medicine
Admission 01/08/2024  Discharge 01/12/2024
Patient: Jada Simmons  DOB 09/08/2001
Allergies: NKDA

Admitting diagnosis: acute asthma exacerbation with hypercapnic respiratory failure

History: 22 yo with lifelong asthma on fluticasone and albuterol, adherence by her report irregular, brought in overnight by EMS with 2 days of worsening wheeze after a cold. Failed to improve with back-to-back nebulizers and IV steroids in the ED and was intubated there.

Hospital course: Admitted to the MICU on the ventilator. Treated with scheduled bronchodilators and IV corticosteroids. Rapid improvement; extubated on hospital day 2 without difficulty. Transferred to the floor, weaned to room air, ambulating without desaturation by discharge. No pneumonia on imaging.

Discharge medications:
- prednisone 40 mg daily x 5 days
- fluticasone propionate HFA 220 mcg 1 puff twice daily (continue)
- albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h prn
- levocetirizine 5 mg daily prn

Instructions: take the controller every day. Follow up with PCP within 1 week.
Discharging physician: hospitalist

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after her admission 1/8-1/12 at the regional hospital, discharge summary reviewed. She was intubated in their ED for a severe asthma flare that started with a cold, extubated the next day. Finished the 5 days of prednisone yesterday. Back at work Saturday. Says she was scared, first time on a breathing machine.

Now: mild cough in the mornings, no night waking this week, albuterol once or twice a day, less each day. Taking fluticasone twice a day since discharge.

Exam: comfortable, full sentences. Lungs clear, no wheeze, normal expiratory phase. Heart regular.

A/P: Severe persistent asthma, recovering after a near-fatal exacerbation needing intubation. Regimen unchanged per discharge plan; long talk about using the controller daily, not just after flares. She has a peak flow meter, encouraged to start using it again. Written instructions on when to go to the ED: albuterol not lasting 4 hours, can't speak full sentences. Recheck 3 months.

documents.title: peak flow
documents.author: patient
documents.body: started doing the peak flow thing again like you said. what number am i supposed to worry about

documents.title: RE: peak flow
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great that you're using it. For the next 2 weeks, do it each morning when you feel well and write down the best number you get. That becomes your personal best. Bring the log to your April visit and we'll write your zones on your action plan. Until then, the rule is the same: if albuterol isn't lasting 4 hours or you can't talk in full sentences, go to the ED.

documents.title: No-show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 10:00. Called, she picked up a double shift and forgot. Rebooked 4/23.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Asthma Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Asthma check. Since the hospital she has been more regular with fluticasone, 'most days', but slipped some over the last month. Spring pollen starting; some sneezing, taking levocetirizine. Albuterol 2-3 times a week, no night waking, no ED or urgent care since January.
O: well. Lungs clear bilaterally. Nasal mucosa a bit boggy.
A/P: Severe persistent asthma, fair control. Same plan, daily controller, albuterol as needed. Rhinitis: levocetirizine daily through the season rather than as needed. Physical in August.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx refill request for fluticasone propionate HFA 220 mcg and levocetirizine. Last OV 4/23/2024. Approved per protocol, 1 inhaler with 2 refills; levocetirizine 30 days with 2 refills.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22 yo here for yearly physical.

Interval: no hospital or ED visits since January. Asthma 'okay this summer'; uses albuterol about twice a week, fluticasone 'most days' (honestly closer to every other day when she works closing shifts). No nocturnal symptoms. Allergies quiet in summer.
Gyn: sees an outside gynecology office for women's health; no contraception from us. LMP 2 weeks ago, regular.
SH: unchanged, never smoker, weekend drinks 1-2. Still uninsured; Medicaid application stalled waiting for a pay stub, gave her the navigator's number.
ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Lungs clear. Heart RRR without murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without edema. Skin without rash.

A/P
- Health maintenance: CBC/CMP today. Pap not due until fall 2025 (normal 10/2022). Flu and updated COVID in October. Tdap current (2019). HPV complete.
- Asthma: controller adherence again. She is willing to set a phone alarm. Continue current inhalers.
- PHQ-2 0.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Afebrile. Influenza (trivalent) L deltoid, Moderna updated COVID R deltoid. Tolerated, waited 15 min, left feeling fine.

documents.title: Triage call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling: burning with urination, going more often, and yellow discharge for about 2 days. No fever, no back pain, no pelvic pain she can describe. Offered same-day visit here today. She already has an appointment Monday 12/23 with her outside gynecologist and would rather go there since they do her exams. Advised to keep it, avoid intercourse until seen, call back or go to urgent care for fever, flank pain or worse pain over the weekend. She agreed. Will ask the gyn office to send us their note.

documents.title: Gynecology visit letter (received 12/27/2024)
documents.author: obstetrics and gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Visit date: 12/23/2024
Re: Jada Simmons, DOB 09/08/2001
Allergies: NKDA

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Simmons for five days of burning with urination, frequency, and a yellow vaginal discharge. Over the past month she has had unprotected intercourse with more than one partner.

Her history includes severe persistent asthma and allergic rhinitis. Medications: albuterol inhaler as needed, fluticasone 220 mcg inhaler twice daily (she tells me she misses doses), levocetirizine as needed. No surgeries.

Vital signs were normal. On speculum exam there was purulent discharge from the cervical os, and bimanual exam elicited cervical motion tenderness. No adnexal mass.

Urine hCG negative. Urinalysis not suggestive of urinary infection. Cervical NAAT came back positive for gonorrhea and negative for chlamydia. HIV antigen/antibody and RPR were both negative.

Impression: gonococcal cervicitis; high-risk sexual exposure.

Plan: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given in the office, plus doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for seven days started empirically before the chlamydia result returned (she is to finish it). Abstain until treatment complete and partners treated; partner referral information given and the case reported as required. Condom counseling. Return in three months for repeat testing.

Sincerely,
Attending gynecologist
